paper_metadata.title: Development of low-density γ/γ′ Co-Al-Ta-based superalloys with high solvus temperature

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The present paper reports the development of W -, Mo-, and V -free and Ni - and Cr-containing Co-Al-Ta-based superalloys.

evidence.section: 2.1 Sample preparation
evidence.quote: Small button ingots (~30 g) were arc-melted (under a high-purity Ar atmosphere) using raw materials of Co, Al, Ta, Ni, and Cr (a purity of at least 99.9 wt.%).

evidence.section: 2.1 Sample preparation
evidence.quote: A solution treatment at 1300 °C for 24 h was performed for all samples before annealing at lower temperatures.

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: Figure 1(a) shows the microstructure of Co-12Al-2Ta alloy ( at.%, referred to as base alloy) heat-treated at 800 °C for 48 h.

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: the cube-shaped γ′ phase could be readily observed

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: compositions of the γ′ and γ phases are Co-17.6 ± 2.3Al-5.0 ± 0.2Ta and Co-8.3 ± 2.8Al-0.6 ± 0.1Ta, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: a small amount of CoAl phase was formed in the grain interior

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: the solvus temperature obtained in the base alloy (~949 °C) is comparable to those of Co-9Al-7.5W (~990 °C) [4] and Co-5Al-14V (~964 °C) [ 36] ternary alloys .

evidence.section: 3.1 Metastable γ′-Co3(Al, Ta) phase with the L12 structure
evidence.quote: An Akashi MVK -H1 hardness test machine was used to measure the hardness of the studied alloys at a weight load of 0.5 kg
